group.passage: More than three kilometres below the surface of the Pacific, large areas of the seabed are scattered with potato-sized lumps called nodules, which are rich in the metals needed for electric car batteries. Should companies be allowed to collect them? Here are eight comments from miners, scientists and fishers.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Ana, tuna fisher
passage_parts.text: Our boats work the very waters where the mining ships would operate. If the companies can prove that the mud they pump back into the sea will stay far below the depths where tuna feed, I will not stand in their way.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Kai, mining engineer
passage_parts.text: Every electric car battery needs nickel and cobalt, and today most of these metals come from mines on land, which have brought destruction to rainforests in several countries. The nodules simply lie loose on the seabed, waiting to be picked up, so the choice seems obvious to me.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Dr. Chen, ocean chemist
passage_parts.text: I am not against mining in principle. Show me a plan that leaves large parts of the seabed untouched and keeps a close watch on the clouds of mud, and I will be the first to sign it.

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: Mr. Park, battery maker
passage_parts.text: Some of my colleagues say they would welcome metals from the seabed if prices fell far enough. I disagree, because we are already learning to recycle old batteries and to make new ones with less cobalt, so the seabed may never be needed at all.

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Dr. Lopez, marine biologist
passage_parts.text: We have described only a small share of the animals that live down there, and almost every survey turns up new species. Marks made on the seabed during a test decades ago are still easy to see, and far fewer animals live there than before.

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Leilani, island fisher
passage_parts.text: Some people on my island say that mining would be worth it if it brought well-paid jobs. But the ocean has fed my family for generations, and no amount of money could ever replace it.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Tomas, deckhand on a test ship
passage_parts.text: The pay is good, and my family needs it. Still, I have seen how much dirty water we pour over the side of the ship every day. Clean that up, and I will defend this work to anyone.

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Prof. Adams, economist
passage_parts.text: Even supporters admit that nobody knows how long the effects would last. Starting now would be a leap in the dark, and I doubt that we will ever be able to make it safe.

questions.stem: Which phrase does Prof. Adams use to describe “an action whose results no one can predict”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: 支持採礦的 Kai 說，電池需要的鎳和鈷現在大多來自陸地上的礦場，這些礦場已經在好幾個國家對雨林造成破壞（brought destruction to rainforests）。摘要句 picking up nodules ... is far kinder to nature than ___ rainforests to dig metals out of the ground 中，than 後面和句首的動名詞 picking up 對比，要填動名詞，而且要能以 rainforests 當受詞；把名詞 destruction 轉成動詞 destroy，再加 -ing 成為 destroying。
evidence: Every electric car battery needs nickel and cobalt, and today most of these metals come from mines on land, which have brought destruction to rainforests in several countries.
1.strategy_zh: than ___ rainforests：和句首的 picking up 比較，要填動名詞，並且能以 rainforests 當受詞。找支持者 Kai 說陸地礦場對雨林帶來了什麼，把那個名詞轉成動詞再加 -ing。
hints: than 後面和 picking up 對比：要填動名詞。
Kai 說陸地上的礦場對雨林造成了什麼？
destruction 的動詞是 destroy，再加 -ing。

2.explanation_zh: Lopez 博士說，住在深海的動物我們只描述過一小部分（We have described only a small share of the animals），幾乎每次調查都會發現新物種。摘要句 much of the life on the seabed still awaits ___, so some creatures may vanish before science has even named them 中，空格在動詞 awaits 之後當受詞，要填名詞；把動詞 describe 改成名詞 description：海床上的許多生物還在「等待被描述」，也就是科學界還不認識它們。
evidence: We have described only a small share of the animals that live down there, and almost every survey turns up new species.
2.strategy_zh: still awaits ___：await（等待）後面接名詞當受詞；後半句 before science has even named them 說明科學界還沒認識這些生物。找生物學家說「我們只做到一小部分」的那個動詞，改成名詞。
hints: Lopez 博士說深海的動物，我們只對其中一小部分做了什麼？
把動詞 describe 改成名詞 description。

3.explanation_zh: 題目問哪些留言者願意接受深海採礦，但只在某些條件達成時。(A) Ana 說如果公司能證明打回海裡的泥漿會停留在鮪魚覓食的深度之下，她就不會阻擋，可推知條件達成她才接受。(C) 陳博士說自己原則上不反對採礦，只要有計畫能保留大片不受干擾的海床、並密切監測泥雲，就會第一個簽名，用「給我看…，我就…」的句型表示條件。(G) Tomas 說薪水好、家人需要，但他看過船每天把多少髒水倒進海裡；只要把這件事處理好，他就會向任何人捍衛這份工作，用「祈使句＋and」表示條件。其餘：(B) Kai 無條件支持，認為該怎麼選再明顯不過；(D) Park 先生提到同事「如果價格夠低」就歡迎海床金屬，但條件是同事的，他本人不同意，認為回收與少鈷電池可能讓海床根本用不著；(F) Leilani 提到島上有人說「如果能帶來高薪工作」就值得，但她本人認為大海養活她家好幾代，多少錢都無法取代；(E) Lopez 博士和 (H) Adams 教授都反對，一個擔心深海生物還沒被認識就受害、試驗區幾十年後動物仍少得多，一個認為現在開始是後果難料的冒險，而且懷疑永遠無法讓它變得安全。
evidence: If the companies can prove that the mud they pump back into the sea will stay far below the depths where tuna feed, I will not stand in their way.
Show me a plan that leaves large parts of the seabed untouched and keeps a close watch on the clouds of mud, and I will be the first to sign it.
Clean that up, and I will defend this work to anyone.
Some of my colleagues say they would welcome metals from the seabed if prices fell far enough.
I disagree, because we are already learning to recycle old batteries and to make new ones with less cobalt, so the seabed may never be needed at all.
Some people on my island say that mining would be worth it if it brought well-paid jobs.
But the ocean has fed my family for generations, and no amount of money could ever replace it.

option_notes_zh.B: Kai 無條件支持：陸地礦場破壞雨林，結核就散在海床上等人撿，他認為「該怎麼選再明顯不過」，沒有附帶任何條件。
option_notes_zh.D: 帶條件句的誘答：「如果價格降得夠低就歡迎」是同事的看法，Park 先生說 I disagree，認為靠回收與少鈷電池，也許根本不需要海床。
option_notes_zh.E: Lopez 博士反對：深海動物大多還沒被描述，幾十年前的試驗區至今痕跡清楚、動物少得多；Lopez 博士沒有提出任何可以接受的條件。
option_notes_zh.F: 帶條件句的誘答：「如果能帶來高薪工作就值得」是島上其他人的說法，Leilani 用 But 反駁，認為大海養活她家好幾代，多少錢都無法取代。
option_notes_zh.H: Adams 教授反對：現在開始是後果難料的冒險，而且他懷疑我們永遠無法讓它變得安全，等於否定了任何條件。

3.strategy_zh: 條件立場題：每一則先判斷作者本人支持或反對，再看支持是否附帶條件。條件不一定用 if：Show me…, and I will…、Clean that up, and I will… 這類「祈使句＋and」也表示條件。帶 if 的句子要確認條件是誰的看法、作者最後同不同意。
hints: 每一則都問：作者本人支持採礦嗎？有沒有附帶條件？
C 和 G 沒有用 if，但「祈使句＋and I will…」是什麼意思？
D 和 F 的 if 句是作者自己的條件，還是轉述別人的看法？

A: If the companies can prove that the mud they pump back into the sea will stay far below the depths where tuna feed, I will not stand in their way.
B: The nodules simply lie loose on the seabed, waiting to be picked up, so the choice seems obvious to me.
C: Show me a plan that leaves large parts of the seabed untouched and keeps a close watch on the clouds of mud, and I will be the first to sign it.
D: Some of my colleagues say they would welcome metals from the seabed if prices fell far enough.
I disagree, because we are already learning to recycle old batteries and to make new ones with less cobalt, so the seabed may never be needed at all.
E: Marks made on the seabed during a test decades ago are still easy to see, and far fewer animals live there than before.
F: Some people on my island say that mining would be worth it if it brought well-paid jobs.
But the ocean has fed my family for generations, and no amount of money could ever replace it.
G: Clean that up, and I will defend this work to anyone.
H: Starting now would be a leap in the dark, and I doubt that we will ever be able to make it safe.

4.explanation_zh: a leap in the dark 字面是「在黑暗中跳躍」，引申為「結果難以預料的冒險行動」，正是題幹 an action whose results no one can predict 的意思。Adams 教授說現在就開始採礦是一場後果難料的冒險，而且他懷疑我們永遠無法讓它變得安全。答案保留文中的名詞片語 a leap in the dark（冠詞 a 可省略）。
evidence: Starting now would be a leap in the dark, and I doubt that we will ever be able to make it safe.
4.strategy_zh: 題幹限定 Adams 教授，並用文中沒有的 action、results、predict 描述概念；找他用來形容「現在就開始採礦」的名詞片語，只寫片語本身，不要連 Starting now would be 一起抄。
hints: 先找 Adams 教授怎麼形容「現在就開始」這件事。
Starting now would be ___：後面是一個和「黑暗」有關的名詞片語。
答案五個字，以 a leap 開頭。

translation_zh.text:
在太平洋海面下三公里多的深處，大片海床散布著馬鈴薯大小、稱為「結核」的團塊，富含電動車電池所需的金屬。應該允許公司去採集它們嗎？以下是礦業人士、科學家和漁民的八則留言。

(A) Ana，鮪魚漁民：我們的漁船作業的海域，正是採礦船將來要作業的地方。如果這些公司能證明他們打回海裡的泥漿，會一直停留在鮪魚覓食的深度之下很遠的地方，我就不會阻擋他們。
(B) Kai，採礦工程師：每一顆電動車電池都需要鎳和鈷，而現在這些金屬大多來自陸地上的礦場，這些礦場已經在好幾個國家對雨林造成破壞。結核就散落在海床上，等著被撿起來，所以對我來說，該怎麼選再明顯不過。
(C) 陳博士，海洋化學家：我原則上並不反對採礦。給我看一個能讓大片海床維持原狀、並密切監測泥雲的計畫，我會第一個簽名。
(D) Park 先生，電池製造商：我有些同事說，如果價格降得夠低，他們會歡迎來自海床的金屬。我不同意，因為我們已經在學習回收舊電池、製造用鈷更少的新電池，所以也許根本不需要動到海床。
(E) Lopez 博士，海洋生物學家：住在深海的動物，我們只描述過一小部分，而且幾乎每次調查都會發現新物種。幾十年前試驗時在海床上留下的痕跡至今仍清楚可見，那裡的動物也比以前少得多。
(F) Leilani，島上的漁民：我們島上有些人說，如果採礦能帶來高薪的工作，那就值得。但大海養活我們家好幾代了，多少錢都無法取代它。
(G) Tomas，試驗船的甲板水手：薪水很好，我的家人也需要這份收入。不過，我親眼看過我們每天從船邊倒出去多少髒水。把這件事處理好，我會向任何人捍衛這份工作。
(H) Adams 教授，經濟學家：就連支持者都承認，沒有人知道影響會持續多久。現在就開始，等於在黑暗中跳躍、後果難料，而且我懷疑我們永遠沒辦法讓它變得安全。

checked.claim: More than three kilometres below the surface of the Pacific, the seabed is scattered with potato-sized lumps called nodules.
The nodules are rich in the metals needed for electric car batteries (nickel, cobalt, manganese).
Kai: “Every electric car battery needs nickel and cobalt.” — overstated: the fact sheet says some battery types (lithium iron phosphate) contain no cobalt or nickel.
Most of these metals now come from mines on land, which have been linked to rainforest destruction.
The nodules lie loose on the seabed.
Mining waters overlap tuna fishing grounds, and mud/waste released into the sea could affect where tuna feed (Ana).
Mining would release clouds of mud (sediment-laden water) (Dr. Chen, Tomas).
Battery makers are learning to recycle old batteries and to make batteries with less cobalt (Mr. Park).
Only a small share of deep-sea animals has been described, and almost every survey turns up new species (Dr. Lopez).
Marks made in a test decades ago are still visible, and far fewer animals live there (Dr. Lopez).

problems: 留言 (B) Kai 的「Every electric car battery needs nickel and cobalt」與事實單 f10（磷酸鋰鐵電池不含鈷、鎳）不符；是支持採礦者的誇大說法，而且 (D) Park 先生的留言提出反面說法，沒有任何小題考這一點；這一句同時是第 1 格的證據句（考的是後半句 brought destruction to rainforests）。不影響作答，列 warn；改版時建議改成 Most electric car batteries need nickel and cobalt。
